issues: The assigned character label “Nephite armies of Moroni” is not established for this passage; the text only says Mormon was given command of the Nephites’ armies. The scene can show Mormon among the Nephites, but their identities as Moroni’s armies are uncertain.

“Nephite armies of Moroni” and “Lamanite warriors (Enos to Alma era)” are not labels established for the armies in this passage; the text identifies them only as Nephites and Lamanites. Depicting defenders and attackers is supported, but their specific army identities are uncertain.

The source says un-gathered lands were destroyed and their towns, villages, and cities burned, but does not specify that the destruction was by fire beyond the settlements being burned. Showing a settlement burning is supported; showing the destruction of the lands themselves is less visually specified.
“Nephite inhabitants” is not explicitly named as a character group in this verse; the text mentions inhabitants without specifying who is present in a scene.

“Nephite armies of Moroni” and “Lamanite warriors (Enos to Alma era)” are not established as the identities of the combatants here; the text names only Nephites and Lamanites. The much larger force pressing the Nephites back is a reasonable visual inference, but specific formations or equipment are unspecified.

The listed army labels are not established for this passage; the text names Nephites and Lamanites generally. Showing some Nephites escaping and others overtaken is a reasonable inference, but the precise manner of destruction is unspecified.

The verse contrasts the people's former and current state, but does not establish a specific present-time staging or visual appearance. The proposed narration-only treatment is conservative and avoids depicting the figurative shepherd, chaff, vessel, or divine and satanic figures.

The scene's warning that the remnant may go among the Gentiles as a lion and tear them in pieces is in the source, but treating this imagery as figurative is a conservative visual choice; the verse does not specify its visual realization. No present attack or divine appearance should be added. The separately mentioned earth rolled together as a scroll is likewise not a present event.
